claim: The Service Quotas default for All Standard (A, C, D, H, I, M, R, T, Z) Spot Instance Requests is 5, and the quota is adjustable; Spot Instance quotas are per AWS account per Region and are managed in vCPUs.

qualifiers.scope: per account, per Region; measured in vCPUs
qualifiers.condition: Standard families A, C, D, H, I, M, R, T, Z; EC2 adjusts the quota automatically based on usage

evidence.quote: | All Standard (A, C, D, H, I, M, R, T, Z) Spot Instance Requests | 5 | [Yes](https://console.aws.amazon.com/servicequotas/home/services/ec2/quotas/L-34B43A08) |
There are quotas for the number of running Spot Instances and pending Spot Instance requests per AWS account per Region.

Spot Instance quotas are managed in terms of the *number of virtual central processing units (vCPUs)* that your running Spot Instances are either using or will use pending the fulfillment of open Spot Instance requests.
Even though Amazon EC2 automatically adjusts your Spot Instance quotas based on your usage, you can request a quota increase if necessary.
